key_insight: ApexGO leverages generative AI to redesign peptide antibiotics that more effectively kill drug‑resistant bacteria; top candidates were validated in laboratory assays and mouse infection models, matching or outperforming standard antibiotics.
problem_solved: Efficiently explores and optimizes peptide sequence space to find potent, low‑toxicity antibiotics against drug‑resistant bacteria, reducing the time and cost of traditional iterative wet‑lab discovery.
method: Generative model proposes peptide sequence variants guided by objectives (antimicrobial potency, safety proxies).
In silico scoring and filtering prioritize candidates for synthesis.
Experimental validation pipeline: in vitro antimicrobial assays followed by mouse infection studies to confirm efficacy.
impact: Demonstrates a practical, end‑to‑end ML → wet‑lab workflow for biologics discovery, highlighting how generative models can accelerate antibiotic optimization and bridge computational proposals with in vivo validation—useful template for ML practitioners in drug design.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: generative model → scoring/filters → synthesis → in vitro → in vivo.
Bar chart comparing bacterial kill rates or MICs of ApexGO peptides vs standard antibiotics.
Sequence landscape or embedding scatterplot showing generated diversity and optimized clusters.
Flow/timeline showing rounds from design to mouse efficacy results (decision points and validation milestones).
paper_title: A generative artificial intelligence approach for peptide antibiotic optimization
paper_authors: Marcelo D. T. Torres, Yimeng Zeng, Fangping Wan, Natalie Maus, Jacob Gardner
